unit.why: A brief first-person memorate: the author recalls his first visit to R. Moshe of Savran, who argued with him that one must travel to the great men of the generation rather than rely on one's own reason, supported by exegesis of verses; the teaching dominates and the narrative frame is thin.
unit.boundary_note: excerpt quoted from another book (שושנים אות כ"ז) inside an anthology chain of sources on travelling to the tzaddik

stories.start_quote: הנה בהיותי פעם ראשונה אצל אדמו״ר
stories.summary_en: On the narrator's first visit to R. Moshe of Savran, the rebbe argued at length with him that no one should choose a path of divine service by his own intellect, but should travel to the great men of the generation to be guided, interpreting Ecclesiastes and Proverbs verses to this effect.

tags.why: the content is mainly a teaching with verse exegesis inside a thin narrative frame
